name: Buenos Aires
author: hernang87
description:
Modeled commuter demand for the Buenos Aires metropolitan area (CABA and 39 partidos), built from INDEC Census 2022 at census-radio level (18,018 radios). Employed residents (Ocupado) are the trip producers; total residential population is not used as demand.

Destinations come from the CEP XXI/SIPA 2022 geocoded formal-establishment dataset (coordinates rounded to 0.001 degrees; employment bands converted to capacities: 1-9 = 5, 10-49 = 29.5, 50-199 = 124.5, 200-499 = 349.5, 500+ = 500). The formal layer holds 4,127,148 modeled jobs; the remaining 3,667,547 employed residents are modeled as local residual employment at their residential origins because the source does not locate those jobs. The source excludes informal, self-employed, domestic and uncovered public employment.

Formal workplace capacity is balanced against employed-resident origins with a 12 km doubly constrained gravity model, then projected onto a sparse exact transportation solution that preserves every origin and workplace total. Results are exported as 6,000 adaptive display clusters built from the census radios (workplaces are assigned to their nearest radio), not as individual establishments. Population records are capped at 200 people; a point may hold more residents or jobs. Within CABA, cluster positions use residential parcels from the city's 2022-2024 land-use survey weighted by floor count: a spatial proxy, not parcel-level resident counts. These are modeled commuter flows, not observed commutes.

OpenStreetMap supplies roads, airports, parks and place labels; building footprints come from Overture Maps.
data_source: INDEC Census 2022; CEP XXI/SIPA 2022; GCBA cadastral parcels and 2022–2024 land-use survey
